title: Finance Lease Subsequent Accounting
description: Calculate interest, lease liability reduction and amortization of the right-of-use asset.
html:
What happens after commencement?

For a finance lease, interest accrues on the outstanding lease liability.

When a lease payment is made, part of the payment represents interest and the remainder reduces the lease liability.

The basic roll-forward

Interest = Beginning Lease Liability × Periodic Discount Rate
Liability Reduction = Lease Payment − Interest
Ending Lease Liability = Beginning Liability − Liability Reduction

Example

Assume the beginning lease liability is $50,000.

The annual discount rate is 6% and the year-end lease payment is $12,000.

Step 1 — Interest

$50,000 × 6% = $3,000

Step 2 — Liability reduction

$12,000 − $3,000 = $9,000

Step 3 — Ending liability

$50,000 − $9,000 = $41,000
Beginning Lease Liability $50,000
Interest $3,000
Cash Payment ($12,000)
Ending Lease Liability $41,000

Another way to see the roll-forward

$50,000 + $3,000 − $12,000 = $41,000

Right-of-use asset

For a finance lease, the ROU asset is generally amortized separately from the interest recognized on the lease liability.

The appropriate amortization period depends on the facts, including whether ownership transfers or a purchase option is reasonably certain to be exercised.

Finance lease pattern

  • Interest expense is recognized on the lease liability.
  • The lease payment reduces the liability after interest.
  • The ROU asset is amortized separately.

quiz.prompt: A finance lease has a beginning lease liability of $80,000. The annual discount rate is 5%, and a $18,000 payment is made at year-end. What is the ending lease liability?

objectives: Explain finance lease subsequent accounting and its underlying principles.
Apply the topic to a financial-reporting scenario.
